    21→%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
    22→%% Purpose: Handles an ssh connection, e.i. both the
    23→%% setup SSH Transport Layer Protocol (RFC 4253), Authentication
    24→%% Protocol (RFC 4252) and SSH connection Protocol (RFC 4255)
    25→%% Details of the different protocols are
    26→%% implemented in ssh_transport.erl, ssh_auth.erl and ssh_connection.erl
    27→%% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    28→
    29→-module(ssh_fsm_userauth_server).
    30→-moduledoc false.
    31→
    32→-include("ssh.hrl").
    33→-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
    34→-include("ssh_auth.hrl").
    35→-include("ssh_connect.hrl").
    36→
    37→-include("ssh_fsm.hrl").
    38→
    39→%%====================================================================
    40→%%% Exports
    41→%%====================================================================
    42→
    43→%%% Behaviour callbacks
    44→-export([callback_mode/0, handle_event/4, terminate/3,
    45→	 format_status/2, code_change/4]).
    46→
    47→%%====================================================================
    48→%% gen_statem callbacks
    49→%%====================================================================
    50→
    51→callback_mode() ->
    52→    [handle_event_function,
    53→     state_enter].
    54→
    55→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→
    57→%%% ######## {userauth, server} ####
    58→%%---- userauth request to server
    59→handle_event(internal, 
    60→	     Msg = #ssh_msg_userauth_request{service = ServiceName,
    61→                                             method = Method},
    62→	     StateName = {userauth,server},
    63→	     D0 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh0}) ->
    64→
    65→    case {ServiceName, Ssh0#ssh.service, Method} of
    66→	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", "none"} ->
    67→	    %% Probably the very first userauth_request but we deny unauthorized login
    68→            %% However, we *may* accept unauthorized login if instructed so
    69→            case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
    70→                {not_authorized, _, {Reply,Ssh}} ->
    71→                    D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
    72→                    {keep_state, D};
    73→                {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
    74→                    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
    75→                    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
    76→                     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
    77→                      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
    78→                     ]
    79→                    }
    80→                     
    81→            end;
    82→	
    83→	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", Method} ->
    84→	    %% Userauth request with a method like "password" or so
    85→	    case lists:member(Method, Ssh0#ssh.userauth_methods) of
    86→		true ->
    87→		    %% Yepp! we support this method
    88→		    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
    89→			{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
    90→                            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
    91→                            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
    92→                             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
    93→                              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
    94→                             ]};
    95→			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} when Method == "keyboard-interactive" ->
    96→			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
    97→                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
    98→			    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive,server}, D};
    99→			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   100→			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
   101→                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   102→			    {keep_state, D}
   103→		    end;
   104→		false ->
   105→		    %% No we do not support this method (=/= none)
   106→		    %% At least one non-erlang client does like this. Retry as the next event
   107→		    {keep_state_and_data,
   108→		     [{next_event, internal, Msg#ssh_msg_userauth_request{method="none"}}]
   109→		    }
   110→	    end;
   111→
   112→	%% {"ssh-connection", Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
   113→	%% {ServiceName,      Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
   114→
   115→	{ServiceName, _, _} when ServiceName =/= "ssh-connection" ->
   116→            {Shutdown, D} =  
   117→                ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE,
   118→                                 io_lib:format("Unknown service: ~p",[ServiceName]),
   119→                                 StateName, D0),
   120→            {stop, Shutdown, D}
   121→    end;
   122→
   123→handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive, server}, D0) ->
   124→    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response(Msg, D0#data.ssh_params) of
   125→	{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
   126→            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
   127→            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
   128→             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
   129→              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
   130→             ]};
   131→	{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   132→	    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
   133→            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   134→	    {next_state, {userauth,server}, D};
   135→
   136→	{authorized_but_one_more, _User,  {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   137→            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   138→	    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra,server}, D}
   139→    end;
   140→
   141→handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra, server}, D0) ->
   142→    {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} =
   143→        ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response({extra,Msg}, D0#data.ssh_params),
   144→    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
   145→    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
   146→     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
   147→      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
   148→     ]
   149→    };
   150→
   151→
   152→%%% ######## UNHANDLED EVENT!
   153→handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D) ->
   154→    ssh_connection_handler:handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D).
   155→
   156→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→format_status(A, B) ->
   158→    ssh_connection_handler:format_status(A, B).
   159→
   160→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→terminate(Reason, StateName, D) ->
   162→    ssh_connection_handler:terminate(Reason, StateName, D).
   163→
   164→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   165→code_change(_OldVsn, StateName, State, _Extra) ->
   166→    {ok, StateName, State}.
   167→
   168→%%====================================================================
   169→%% Internal functions
   170→%%====================================================================
   171→
   172→connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0) ->
   173→    D1 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh} =
   174→        ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh1}),
   175→    ssh_connection_handler:handshake(ssh_connected, D1),
   176→    connected_fun(User, Method, D1),
   177→    D1#data{auth_user=User,
   178→            %% Note: authenticated=true MUST NOT be sent
   179→            %% before send_msg!
   180→            ssh_params = Ssh#ssh{authenticated = true}}.
   181→
   182→
   183→set_max_initial_idle_timeout(#data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts=Opts}}) ->
   184→    {{timeout,max_initial_idle_time}, ?GET_OPT(max_initial_idle_time,Opts), none}.
   185→
   186→connected_fun(User, Method, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{peer = {_,Peer}}} = D) ->
   187→    ?CALL_FUN(connectfun,D)(User, Peer, Method).
   188→
   189→
   190→retry_fun(_, undefined, _) ->
   191→    ok;
   192→retry_fun(User, Reason, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts = Opts,
   193→						peer = {_,Peer}
   194→					       }}) ->
   195→    {Tag,Info} =
   196→	case Reason of
   197→	    {error, Error} ->
   198→		{failfun, Error};
   199→	    _ ->
   200→		{infofun, Reason}
   201→	end,
   202→    Fun = ?GET_OPT(Tag, Opts),
   203→    try erlang:fun_info(Fun, arity)
   204→    of
   205→	{arity, 2} -> %% Backwards compatible
   206→	    catch Fun(User, Info);
   207→	{arity, 3} ->
   208→	    catch Fun(User, Peer, Info);
   209→	_ ->
   210→	    ok
   211→    catch
   212→	_:_ ->
   213→	    ok
   214→    end.
   215→

    23→%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
    24→%% Purpose: Details of connection protocol
    25→%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
    26→
    27→-module(ssh_connection).
    28→-moduledoc """
    29→This module provides API functions to send SSH Connection Protocol events to the
    30→other side of an SSH channel.
    31→
    32→The [SSH Connection Protocol (RFC 4254)](http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4254.txt) is used by
    33→clients and servers, that is, SSH channels, to communicate over the SSH
    34→connection. The API functions in this module send SSH Connection Protocol
    35→events, which are received as messages by the remote channel handling the remote
    36→channel. The Erlang format of thoose messages is (see also
    37→[below](`t:event/0`)):
    38→
    39→`{ssh_cm,` `t:ssh:connection_ref/0` `,` `t:channel_msg/0` `}`
    40→
    41→If the `m:ssh_client_channel` behavior is used to implement the channel process,
    42→these messages are handled by
    43→[handle_ssh_msg/2](`c:ssh_client_channel:handle_ssh_msg/2`).
    44→""".
    45→-moduledoc(#{titles =>
    46→                 [{type,<<"General">>},
    47→                  {type,<<"Data Transfer">>},
    48→                  {type,<<"Closing a Channel">>},
    49→                  {type,<<"Pseudo-Terminal">>},
    50→                  {type,<<"Environment Variable">>},
    51→                  {type,<<"Shell or Command">>},
    52→                  {type,<<"Window Change">>},
    53→                  {type,<<"Signals">>},
    54→                  {type,<<"Exit Status">>}]}).
    55→
    56→-include("ssh.hrl").
    57→-include("ssh_connect.hrl").
    58→-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
    59→
    60→%% API
    61→-export([session_channel/2, session_channel/4,
    62→	 exec/4, shell/2, subsystem/4, send/3, send/4, send/5, 
    63→	 send_eof/2, adjust_window/3, setenv/5, close/2, reply_request/4,
    64→	 ptty_alloc/3, ptty_alloc/4]).
    65→
    66→%% Potential API currently unsupported and not tested
    67→-export([window_change/4, window_change/6,
    68→	 signal/3, exit_status/3]).
    69→
    70→%% Internal SSH application API
    71→-export([channel_data/5,
    72→         handle_msg/4,
    73→         handle_stop/1,
    74→
    75→         open_channel/4,
    76→
    77→	 channel_adjust_window_msg/2,
    78→	 channel_close_msg/1,
    79→	 channel_open_failure_msg/4,
    80→	 channel_open_msg/5,
    81→	 channel_status_msg/1,
    82→         channel_data_msg/3,
    83→         channel_eof_msg/1,
    84→         channel_failure_msg/1, 
    85→         channel_open_confirmation_msg/4,
    86→         channel_request_msg/4,
    87→         channel_success_msg/1,
    88→
    89→         request_global_msg/3,
    90→	 request_failure_msg/0, 
    91→	 request_success_msg/1,
    92→
    93→         send_environment_vars/3,
    94→
    95→	 encode_ip/1
    96→        ]).
    97→
    98→%% For testing only
    99→-export([encode_pty_opts/1, decode_pty_opts/1]).
   100→
   101→-type connection_ref() :: ssh:connection_ref().
   102→-type channel_id()     :: ssh:channel_id().
   103→
   104→-doc """
   105→The status of a request. Corresponds to the `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_SUCCESS` and
   106→`SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_FAILURE` values in
   107→[RFC 4254, Section 5.4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section-5.4).
   108→""".
   109→-type req_status() :: success | failure .
   110→-doc """
   111→The result of a call.
   112→
   113→If the request reached the peer, was handled and the response reached the
   114→requesting node the `t:req_status/0` is the status reported from the peer.
   115→
   116→If not, the `t:reason/0` indicates what went wrong:
   117→
   118→- **`closed`** - indicates that the channel or connection was closed when trying
   119→  to send the request
   120→
   121→- **`timeout`** - indicates that the operation exceeded a time limit
   122→""".
   123→-type reason() :: closed | timeout .
   124→
   125→-doc(#{}).
   126→-type result() :: req_status() | {error, reason()} .
   127→
   128→-doc """
   129→The valid values are `0` ("normal") and `1` ("stderr"), see
   130→[RFC 4254, Section 5.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#page-8).
   131→""".
   132→-type ssh_data_type_code() :: non_neg_integer(). % Only 0 and 1 are used
   133→
   134→
   135→%%% The SSH Connection Protocol
   136→
   137→-export_type([event/0,
   138→              channel_msg/0,
   139→              want_reply/0,
   140→              data_ch_msg/0,
   141→              eof_ch_msg/0,
   142→              signal_ch_msg/0,
   143→              exit_signal_ch_msg/0,
   144→              exit_status_ch_msg/0,
   145→              closed_ch_msg/0,
   146→              env_ch_msg/0,
   147→              pty_ch_msg/0,
   148→              shell_ch_msg/0,
   149→              window_change_ch_msg/0,
   150→              exec_ch_msg/0
   151→             ]).
   152→
   153→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   154→-type event() :: {ssh_cm, ssh:connection_ref(), channel_msg()}.
   155→-doc """
   156→As mentioned in the introduction, the
   157→[SSH Connection Protocol](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254) events are
   158→handled as messages. When writing a channel handling process without using the
   159→support by the `m:ssh_client_channel` behavior the process must handle thoose
   160→messages.
   161→""".
   162→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   163→-type channel_msg() ::  data_ch_msg()
   164→                      | eof_ch_msg()
   165→                      | closed_ch_msg()
   166→                      | pty_ch_msg()
   167→                      | env_ch_msg()
   168→                      | shell_ch_msg()
   169→                      | exec_ch_msg()
   170→                      | signal_ch_msg()
   171→                      | window_change_ch_msg()
   172→                      | exit_status_ch_msg()
   173→                      | exit_signal_ch_msg()
   174→                        .
   175→
   176→-doc """
   177→Messages that include a `WantReply` expect the channel handling process to call
   178→[ssh_connection:reply_request/4](`reply_request/4`) with the boolean value of
   179→`WantReply` as the second argument.
   180→""".
   181→-doc(#{title => <<"General">>}).
   182→-type want_reply() :: boolean().
   183→
   184→-doc """
   185→Data has arrived on the channel. This event is sent as a result of calling
   186→[ssh_connection:send/3,4,5](`send/3`).
   187→""".
   188→-doc(#{title => <<"Data Transfer">>,
   189→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.2"}).
   190→-type data_ch_msg() :: {data,
   191→                        ssh:channel_id(),
   192→                        ssh_data_type_code(),
   193→                        Data :: binary()
   194→                       } .
   195→-doc """
   196→Indicates that the other side sends no more data. This event is sent as a result
   197→of calling [ssh_connection:send_eof/2](`send_eof/2`).
   198→""".
   199→-doc(#{title => <<"Closing a Channel">>,
   200→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.3"}).
   201→-type eof_ch_msg() :: {eof,
   202→                       ssh:channel_id()
   203→                      } .
   204→-doc """
   205→A signal can be delivered to the remote process/service using the following
   206→message. Some systems do not support signals, in which case they are to ignore
   207→this message. There is currently no function to generate this event as the
   208→signals referred to are on OS-level and not something generated by an Erlang
   209→program.
   210→""".
   211→-doc(#{title => <<"Signals">>,
   212→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.9"}).
   213→-type signal_ch_msg() :: {signal,
   214→                          ssh:channel_id(),
   215→                          SignalName :: string()
   216→                         } .
   217→-doc """
   218→A remote execution can terminate violently because of a signal. Then this
   219→message can be received. For details on valid string values, see
   220→[RFC 4254](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section-6.10) Section 6.10, which
   221→shows a special case of these signals.
   222→""".
   223→-doc(#{title => <<"Exit Status">>,
   224→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.10"}).
   225→-type exit_signal_ch_msg() :: {exit_signal, ssh:channel_id(),
   226→                               ExitSignal :: string(),
   227→                               ErrorMsg :: string(),
   228→                               LanguageString :: string()} .
   229→-doc """
   230→When the command running at the other end terminates, the following message can
   231→be sent to return the exit status of the command. A zero `exit_status` usually
   232→means that the command terminated successfully. This event is sent as a result
   233→of calling [ssh_connection:exit_status/3](`exit_status/3`).
   234→""".
   235→-doc(#{title => <<"Exit Status">>,
   236→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.10"}).
   237→-type exit_status_ch_msg() :: {exit_status,
   238→                               ssh:channel_id(),
   239→                               ExitStatus :: non_neg_integer()
   240→                              } .
   241→-doc """
   242→This event is sent as a result of calling [ssh_connection:close/2](`close/2`).
   243→Both the handling of this event and sending it are taken care of by the
   244→`m:ssh_client_channel` behavior.
   245→""".
   246→-doc(#{title => <<"Closing a Channel">>,
   247→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 5.3"}).
   248→-type closed_ch_msg() :: {closed,
   249→                          ssh:channel_id()
   250→                         } .
   251→-doc """
   252→Environment variables can be passed to the shell/command to be started later.
   253→This event is sent as a result of calling [ssh_connection:setenv/5](`setenv/5`).
   254→""".
   255→-doc(#{title => <<"Environment Variable">>,
   256→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.4"}).
   257→-type env_ch_msg() :: {env,
   258→                       ssh:channel_id(),
   259→                       want_reply(),
   260→                       Var :: string(),
   261→                       Value :: string()
   262→                      } .
   263→-doc(#{title => <<"Pseudo-Terminal">>,
   264→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.2"}).
   265→-type pty_ch_msg() :: {pty,
   266→                       ssh:channel_id(),
   267→                       want_reply(),
   268→                       {Terminal :: string(),
   269→                        CharWidth :: non_neg_integer(),
   270→                        RowHeight :: non_neg_integer(),
   271→                        PixelWidth :: non_neg_integer(),
   272→                        PixelHeight :: non_neg_integer(),
   273→                        TerminalModes :: [term_mode()]
   274→                       }
   275→                      } .
   276→
   277→-doc """
   278→A pseudo-terminal has been requested for the session. `Terminal` is the value of
   279→the TERM environment variable value, that is, `vt100`. Zero dimension parameters
   280→must be ignored. The character/row dimensions override the pixel dimensions
   281→(when non-zero). Pixel dimensions refer to the drawable area of the window.
   282→`Opcode` in the `TerminalModes` list is the mnemonic name, represented as a
   283→lowercase Erlang atom, defined in
   284→[RFC 4254](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section/8), Section 8. It can
   285→also be an `Opcode` if the mnemonic name is not listed in the RFC. Example:
   286→`OP code: 53, mnemonic name ECHO erlang atom: echo`. This event is sent as a
   287→result of calling [ssh_connection:ptty_alloc/4](`ptty_alloc/4`).
   288→""".
   289→-doc(#{title => <<"Pseudo-Terminal">>,
   290→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.2"}).
   291→-type term_mode() :: {Opcode :: atom() | byte(),
   292→                      Value :: non_neg_integer()} .
   293→
   294→-doc """
   295→This message requests that the user default shell is started at the other end.
   296→This event is sent as a result of calling [ssh_connection:shell/2](`shell/2`).
   297→""".
   298→-doc(#{title => <<"Shell or Command">>,
   299→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.5"}).
   300→-type shell_ch_msg() :: {shell,
   301→                         ssh:channel_id(),
   302→                         want_reply()
   303→                        } .
   304→-doc """
   305→When the window (terminal) size changes on the client side, it _can_ send a
   306→message to the server side to inform it of the new dimensions. No API function
   307→generates this event.
   308→""".
   309→-doc(#{title => <<"Window Change">>,
   310→       rfc => ~"RFC 4254, section 6.7"}).

   401→- **N x [data message(s)](`t:data_ch_msg/0`)** - The result of executing the

   751→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------

   758→-doc false.
   759→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_open_confirmation{recipient_channel = ChannelId, 
   760→					      sender_channel = RemoteId,
   761→					      initial_window_size = WindowSz,
   762→					      maximum_packet_size = PacketSz}, 
   763→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   764→    
   765→    #channel{remote_id = undefined} = Channel =
   766→	ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId), 
   767→    
   768→    ssh_client_channel:cache_update(Cache, Channel#channel{
   769→				     remote_id = RemoteId,
   770→				     recv_packet_size = max(32768, % rfc4254/5.2
   771→							    min(PacketSz, Channel#channel.recv_packet_size)
   772→							   ),
   773→				     send_window_size = WindowSz,
   774→				     send_packet_size = PacketSz}),
   775→    reply_msg(Channel, Connection0, {open, ChannelId});
   776→ 
   777→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_open_failure{recipient_channel = ChannelId,
   778→					 reason = Reason,
   779→					 description = Descr,
   780→					 lang = Lang},  
   781→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   782→    Channel = ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId), 
   783→    ssh_client_channel:cache_delete(Cache, ChannelId),
   784→    reply_msg(Channel, Connection0, {open_error, Reason, Descr, Lang});
   785→
   786→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_success{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   787→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, success);
   788→
   789→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_failure{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   790→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, failure);
   791→
   792→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_eof{recipient_channel = ChannelId}, Connection, _, _SSH) ->
   793→    reply_msg(ChannelId, Connection, {eof, ChannelId});
   794→   
   795→handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_close{recipient_channel = ChannelId},   
   796→	   #connection{channel_cache = Cache} = Connection0, _, _SSH) ->
   797→
   798→	case ssh_client_channel:cache_lookup(Cache, ChannelId) of
   799→		#channel{sent_close = Closed, remote_id = RemoteId,
   800→			 flow_control = FlowControl} = Channel ->
   801→		ssh_client_channel:cache_delete(Cache, ChannelId),
   802→		{CloseMsg, Connection} = 
   803→		    reply_msg(Channel, Connection0, {closed, ChannelId}),
   804→		ConnReplyMsgs =
   805→		    case Closed of
   806→			true -> [];
   807→			false ->
   808→			    RemoteCloseMsg = channel_close_msg(RemoteId),
   809→			    [{connection_reply, RemoteCloseMsg}]
   810→		    end,
   811→
   812→		%% if there was a send() in progress, make it fail
   813→		SendReplyMsgs =
   814→		    case FlowControl of
   815→			undefined -> [];
   816→			From ->
   817→			    [{flow_control, From, {error, closed}}]
   818→		    end,
   819→
   820→		Replies = ConnReplyMsgs ++ CloseMsg ++ SendReplyMsgs,
   821→		{Replies, Connection};
   822→
   823→	    undefined ->
   824→		{[], Connection0}
   825→	end;

  1501→get_window(#channel{send_window_size = 0
  1502→		   } = Channel, Acc) ->
  1503→    {lists:reverse(Acc), Channel};
  1504→get_window(#channel{send_packet_size = 0
  1505→		   } = Channel, Acc) ->

  1507→get_window(#channel{send_buf = Buffer, 
  1508→		    send_packet_size = PacketSize,
  1509→		    send_window_size = WindowSize0
  1510→		   } = Channel, Acc0) ->
  1511→    case queue:out(Buffer) of
  1512→	{{value, {_, Data} = Msg}, NewBuffer} ->
  1513→	    case handle_send_window(Msg, byte_size(Data), PacketSize, WindowSize0, Acc0) of
  1514→		{WindowSize, Acc, {_, <<>>}} ->
  1515→		    {lists:reverse(Acc), Channel#channel{send_window_size = WindowSize,
  1516→							 send_buf = NewBuffer}};
  1517→		{WindowSize, Acc, Rest} ->
  1518→		    get_window(Channel#channel{send_window_size = WindowSize,
  1519→					       send_buf = queue:in_r(Rest, NewBuffer)}, Acc)
  1520→	    end;
  1521→	{empty, NewBuffer} ->
  1522→	    {[], Channel#channel{send_buf = NewBuffer}}
  1523→    end.

  1525→handle_send_window(Msg = {Type, Data}, Size, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) when Size =< WindowSize ->
  1526→    case Size =< PacketSize of
  1527→	true ->
  1528→	    {WindowSize - Size, [Msg | Acc], {Type, <<>>}};
  1529→	false ->
  1530→	    <<Msg1:PacketSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1531→	    {WindowSize - PacketSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}}
  1532→    end;
  1533→handle_send_window({Type, Data}, _, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) when WindowSize =< PacketSize ->
  1534→    <<Msg1:WindowSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1535→    {WindowSize - WindowSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}};
  1536→handle_send_window({Type, Data}, _, PacketSize, WindowSize, Acc) ->
  1537→    <<Msg1:PacketSize/binary, Msg2/binary>> = Data,
  1538→    {WindowSize - PacketSize, [{Type, Msg1} | Acc], {Type, Msg2}}.
